//: SCENARIOS.md, expressed in the same declarative schema playground/scenarios.json uses (see loadScenarios()/normalizeStep() in docs/playground.html for the check-name vocabulary). SCENARIOS.md stays the human-authored source/reference. The starting content for each chapter now lives as a real file under docs/playground/tutorial/ (wired into playground.html's FILE_SOURCES); this file supplies only the SCENARIO-panel body text and quest checklist for each, merged at runtime with playground/scenarios.json.

01-tables.md.body: This table is not verifiable. Change one number and nothing updates. Even if unchanged, no one can guarantee the math is solid.

quest.text: Change any column value or the order total.
Try to tell whether the figures are still correct without doing the math yourself. This is the catch: nothing in this file can confirm it for you.

02-inference.md.body: Inference is a feature where formulas and anchors are detected by VisiMark automatically. Inferred formulas are saved in the document as sheets.

quest.text: Open the Inference tab
Click Infer
Change Qty or Price and watch Total and the order total update automatically
Edit Total directly — VisiMark overwrites it back to the derived value

03-sheets.md.body: A sheet can be written by hand instead of inferred. The name after `#` is the sheet name — it is mandatory whenever a value is anchored in prose, because a document can hold more than one table and sheet.

quest.text: Write `Total = Qty * Price` into the `vmark` block yourself, without using Infer
Change the sheet name after `#` and watch the `OrderTotal` anchor lose its target

04-anchors.md.body: Anchors bind a derived value directly into Markdown prose. They appear as HTML comments and can be placed anywhere in the document, not only directly under a table or sheet — which is why they must name the sheet they belong to.

quest.text: Change Qty or Price and watch Total and the anchored order total update automatically
Type over the anchored 110.00 with a wrong number — VisiMark overwrites it back to the derived value
Change the sheet name after `#` and watch the anchor lose its grip

05-mappers.md.body: Mappers run once per row, or once for a scalar, turning one value into another. `IF(condition, if_true, if_false)` is the one you will reach for most.

quest.text: Add a column rule `Discounted = ROUND(Total * 0.9, 2)` and watch the new column appear
Add `big_order = IF(grand_total > 100, "yes", "no")`, then change Qty until it flips
Try `is_big = grand_total > 100` without IF — VisiMark refuses to store a bare boolean
Add `issued = 2026-01-15` and `due = EOMONTH(issued, 0)`, then change issued and watch due follow

06-aggregates.md.body: Reducers collapse a whole column down to one number. VisiMark ships five: SUM, MIN, MAX, AVG, and COUNT. You have only met SUM so far.

quest.text: Add `average_price = AVG(Price)` and find it in Knowledge next to grand_total
Add `cheapest = MIN(Total)`, `priciest = MAX(Total)`, `line_count = COUNT(Total)`, then add a fourth row
Try `SUM(Price * Qty)` directly, skipping the Total column — VisiMark refuses an expression inside a reducer

07-reasoning.md.body: The REASONING tab shows what `visimark explain` shows: not the numbers, but why each one is what it is — the chain of rules that produces it.

quest.text: Open Reasoning and read how grand_total derives from Total
Change Qty, then compare Reasoning (unchanged) against Knowledge (updated)
Add `tax = ROUND(grand_total * 0.2, 2)` and find it appended to Reasoning, after grand_total

08-knowledge.md.body: The KNOWLEDGE tab shows what `visimark eval --json` shows: the actual computed value behind every cell and scalar in the document, right now.

quest.text: Open Knowledge and find grand_total in the JSON
Change a Price cell and watch Knowledge update immediately
Note the empty assertions array — this document checks no invariant of its own yet

09-units.md.body: Every cell in Price and Total carries the same $ decoration. VisiMark calls this a unit — not a real, convertible unit of measure, just a marking that a column must agree on.

quest.text: Run Build — grand_total is written back as $110.00, not a bare number
Delete the $ from one Price cell and run Build again — VisiMark reports a UNIT error
Change one Total cell's $ to zł instead — same UNIT error, a different mismatch

10-assertions.md.body: An assert states an invariant that must hold, not a value to compute. It has no output of its own — only a pass or a fail.

quest.text: Run Build — Expected and Actual agree, so assert variance == 0 holds
Change one Actual cell so it no longer matches — the assertion fails
Put the number back, then change the assertion to `assert variance > 0` — the same balanced ledger now fails
Open Knowledge and find the assertion's holds value next to variance

11-build-automation.md.body: The BUILD tab runs `visimark check` across every open file at once — the same command a CI pipeline would run against a whole repository, not just the file in front of you.

quest.text: Open Build and click Run Build — every file in FILES gets checked, not just this one
Break something in a different file, switch back here, and Run Build again — it still reports the other file's failure
Fix the mistake and Run Build once more — the status flips back to BUILD PASSING

12-charts.md.body: A chart statement is a generated artifact: fmt draws the SVG from the column(s) it names, and check proves the file on disk still matches the table it was drawn from — the picture can never quietly drift away from the numbers underneath it.

quest.text: Open Reasoning and find the chart declaration
Change a Price or Qty value and watch the bar chart redraw in Preview
Add a fourth row to the table without touching the chart statement — a new bar appears on its own
Change `as bar` to `as pie` in the chart statement — same data, a different picture
